Published online:
September 2, 2026

Geographic focus:
Canada (North America), with secondary reference to US-Canada trade relations

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — references 11 months of unchanged rates, Q2 GDP, prior BoC guidance
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — December hike pricing, inflation trajectory, oil price spillover risk
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — multiple hike scenario into 2027, sustained trade tension impact

Synopsis:
The Bank of Canada held its policy rate at 2.25% but Governor Macklem delivered a hawkish pivot, explicitly signaling willingness to hike multiple times if inflation — currently at 3%, driven largely by elevated oil prices near $90/bbl vs. the BoC's $75 assumption — remains too high. The bank dropped neutral language from its statement. Money markets now price a December hike and ~three additional increases in 2027. US tariffs add uncertainty but are considered a secondary risk to oil-driven inflation.
